speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Okay, if you could please raise your hand if you’d  like a question and just wait for the microphone  
to come. Nizaar. Hi, Calum. Just wondered,  how important was it to get that win today,  
just so you also have a carrot to dangle to the  players for the end of the season, especially  
with Premier League matches to come? Yeah, it  was important to get the win. I’m not sure if  
it was in relation to having an FA Cup final  or a carrot. I think it was important to break  
the momentum and the form that we were in, and I  thought we were confident that we would do that  
today. And I think that completely changes the  feel within the group. I think that was probably  
more important and gives us confidence going into  the next five games. Is there also a motivation to  
win this competition for the fans, because it’s  been a tough season for them, to have different  
managers and this difficult run of form? Do you  kind of think you need to win it for the fans?  
We want to win every game for the fans and every  competition, and it’s unfortunately not worked out  
like that this year, but we want to win every  single game from now to the end of the season,  
as you do in any season. But it’s not extra  motivation. We want to do it for ourselves, we  
want to do it for the fans and the club. Everyone.  Massive competition, the FA Cup, historic,  
and we want to win the final and win every Premier  League game remaining. Thanks, Nizaar. Fourth row,  
please. Calum, congratulations. Enzo scored a big  goal for you at Man City in your first game in  
charge. He scored a big goal for you again today.  Can you tell us what he brings to the team, but  
also to the squad as a leader? I said that to him  at the end. I said, you like scoring at the back  
post for me, and he just laughed. So he does that  really well. He’s done it all year. It’s one of  
his biggest attributes, that when you attack down  the right, his timing of his runs, his ability to  
actually get good distance and height on his jump,  and his heading technique is really good. He’s a  
winner. He’s got so much talent. He’s got so  much fight. He’s massive for this group. And  
the best thing about Enzo is that he can do a bit  of everything. But when it gets tough, you see the  
fight in him. You see him driving the group on,  you see him making tackles, you see him fighting  
for every loose ball. So he was exceptional today  and deserved his man of the match. Dom. Calum,  
another word on Enzo, if you don’t mind. I mean,  you’ve talked about his overall game, but his  
goalscoring has really improved in the last few  seasons. He seems to pop up in bigger games as  
well in that sense. I mean, how impressed are you  with his ability to score important and decisive  
moments for Chelsea? Yeah, it’s something we rely  on a lot. That’s why he’s changed position a lot  
over the last few years. He’s played deeper, he’s  played as a 10, he’s moved about. But I think he’s  
such a threat in the box that the higher up you  play him, and he can drop down and he can drift,  
but the higher up you play him, he can really,  really cause oppositions problems in that left  
half-space and attacking the back stick. Dan.  How do you explain the difference in level of  
performance between Tuesday and today? Because  it felt like night and day. In all honesty, we  
haven’t even looked at the Brighton performance.  We’ve solely focused on, I know it’s a boring  
answer, but we have literally solely focused on  Leeds, what Leeds do, what threats they have,  
how we have to combat that, where we can expose  them. What I thought we’d done really well in  
the first half is that’s literally been our whole  focus, making sure that tactically we’re set up,  
mentally and psychologically we’re ready for  what we’re going to face, because Leeds are a  
very good side that make it very, very tough. And  that’s all we focused on. May I just ask as well,  
there was a bit of a ruck on the touchline after  Robert went down in the penalty area. Seemed to  
be a suggestion that he’d gone down, he might  have been told to go down to sort of take the  
sting out of the game. Can you tell me what  happened there and what was going on on the  
touchline? It seemed to be a bit going on between  the two benches. Oh, I’m unsure about the ruckus,  
in all honesty. I used it as an opportunity to  speak to the players and get some information  
on that we felt was needed. So I’m not aware  of any ruckus. Sorry, Simon. Congrats, Calum.  
Was there any hesitation in your mind to name Enzo  Fernandez captain, given all the noise around him?  
And secondly, after the game, were you sort of  telling the players, this is just the start of  
making good on what’s happened in recent weeks?  The first part of your question was, was there, in  
terms of making Enzo Fernandez captain? I’m very  aware that I’m the interim coach and Enzo is the  
vice-captain of this club, so I wasn’t hesitant  to make him captain, no. Reece James isn’t fit  
to play this game. And your second question  was? Basically sort of telling the players,  
did you say anything to the players afterwards,  that this is just the start? You’ve not done the  
job yet in terms of putting the season right,  as it were. Yeah, we spoke before the game,  
we spoke in the lead-up to the game, sorry,  that we’ve got a minimum of five games left,  
potentially six if we win against Leeds. And it’s  tough in this moment when you’ve been on a losing  
run, but one moment, one result, one performance  can change that. And that’s what we’ve been going  
after in terms of shifting the momentum in the  group. And I did reinforce that at the end. But  
it goes without saying, we’re at Chelsea Football  Club. We need to try and win every game. So that  
is our target from now to the end of the season.  Ed. Hi, Calum. Eight years ago, you were assistant  
manager for Whyteleafe, and today you got to the  FA Cup final. Was it a bit of a pinch-yourself  
moment for yourself before that? I’d worked in  a Europa League club before that, so no, it felt  
normal. You don’t even have time to focus on it.  You don’t take in the fact that you’re playing at  
Wembley. You’re just solely focused on making  sure the team’s performance is at the highest  
level. So you don’t have time to take that all in.  Maybe at the end of the season reality will hit,  
and it’s an unbelievable experience for me, but  there’s so much just coming thick and fast that  
you don’t even have time to take it in, in all  honesty. And you’ve come up against Pep already  
this season. You’re going to face him again in  the final. Do you think you’ve got a chance of  
winning the trophy? Yeah, of course. They’re  a great side. He’s a great manager. They’re  
probably the form team in the league. There’s a  lot, a lot that they can do to hurt you. But we  
wouldn’t be going into the game thinking we’re  not going to win. We’re going to be confident.  
We’re going to attack the game and hopefully put  in that sort of performance again. In the middle,  
please. You brought in Tosin Adarabioyo for the  start of the game. Was that a combination of  
things? Was it his height and his presence in the  air? Was it his leadership? I think I’ve read that  
players refer to him as Uncle Tosin and stuff, one  of the more experienced players. Was it a mix of  
the two things? It’s a really good question. It  was one of the most difficult decisions in the  
preparation for this game, because Jorrel Hato has  been probably our best player over the last five,  
six games. But I decided to go with Tosin mainly  down to the Dominic Calvert-Lewin threat and  
probably being the best match-up to defend that.  Also, set pieces is a massive part of their game.  
Tosin is a great leader, a great character. I  fully trust Jorrel and Jorrel could have played  
in this game, as could Wesley Fofana. So you  make decisions as a manager and you hope you get  
them right. And I thought Tosin was exceptional  today. Okay, thank you so much, guys. Thank you.
title: Calum McFarlane post-match press conference | Chelsea 1-0 Leeds United | FA Cup
